page.layout: One column of italic text, full width, from top to bottom. No margin notes. Catchword "inde" at the right below the last line. A faint mark at the bottom left, not transcribed.

main_text.p: trorsum turpis: hypocritarum & Enthusiastarum, qui obtentu Reformati-onis orbi illudunt, qui sub larva Spiritus carni militant, qui libertatem prophetandi sibi arrogant, ut aliis licentius imponant, quid sibi velint & quo tendant, occulta consilia sapienter perspicere, eorumque conatibus tempestive & prudenter obvenire, τίς πρὸς ταῦτα; Quotusquisque est ea narium sagacitate, ea perspicacia oculorum, ea lacertorum & laterum firmitate, ut ad ista omnia debite peragenda unus sufficiat? Ista si cogitabitis, facile ut opinor & illud una existimabitis, mihi cui omnia jam dicta ex officio incumbunt facienda, omnino sub tam impari onere succumbendum esse, ni vos me fatiscentem usque & languentem[?] cum omni humanitate vestra sub-

page.notes: The Greek phrase "τίς πρὸς ταῦτα" is set in roman type within the italic line. "Quotusquisque" is underlined in the print. The first word "Ista" is preceded by a mark that may be a stray "?"; I read it as "Ista si". "languentem" is uncertain: the print is worn at that point, so [?] is marked. The faint mark at the bottom left is not legible and is left out. No page number or running head is printed.
